title: File:Nant Gwynant - Flickr - Petersrockypics.jpg
author: Petersrockypics
description:
A crisp winter's morning, and a view over Nant gwynant valley to the snow capped peak of Gallt Y Wenallt, a mountain which forms part of the Yr Wyddfa / Snowdon horseshoe.
In the valley below, a building often referred to as "chapel in the valley" on account of its exterior design, but is actually the Cwm dyli hydro-electric power station. Built 1905 and commissioned 1906, it was the largest hydro-electric power station in the United Kingdom. It is also Britain's oldest power station, and is believed to be one of the oldest Grid-connected hydro-electric stations in the world.

title: File:Carneddau Ponies - Flickr - Petersrockypics.jpg
author: Petersrockypics
description:
A young Foal with it's Mother atop Mynydd Y Dref (Conwy mountain) in the foothills of the Carneddau range of mountains.  
Mynydd y Dref is the remains of an ancient volcano that erupted about 450 million years ago.
The view incorporates Conwy marina, Conwy river, Llandudno, Deganwy, Llandudno junction, Penrhynside, Penrhyn bay.
Carneddau ponies are a breed of small Welsh Mountain ponies, present in the Carneddau mountains in north Wales, in Eryri (snowdonia). In 2013, DNA identification revealed that they are a distinct, unique and ancient breed having been isolated in the Carneddau for centuries. "A study of their DNA shows they have been isolated for at least several hundred years, according to researchers at Aberystwyth University."
They can feed themselves in winter by scraping the snow of the grass, a trait shared only with other British isles ponies, but done more often as they get no supplementary feed.
The ponies while semi-feral are owned by 7 local families who once a year-round them up for health checks and to allow some ponies to be sold to keep the herd in balance. In the past the Carneddau ponies were sold for working use e.g. as pit ponies, but now are sold only for leisure.
